niko: kicking off a small canary for raven-v3-8q on staging, focusing on tool-invoke JSON compliance sampling (2% traffic). gonna compare parse failure rates vs 16-bit.
elaine: sounds good. any initial hypotheses on where failures will cluster? :thinking_face:
niko: early guess: token-cutoff and truncated arrays when KV prefix is long; also a slight increase in stray commas and unmatched braces from decoder quirks under 8q.
rajeev: can we capture the raw token stream for failed parses? need to see whether it's decoder hallucination vs truncation.
maria: +1 on raw tokens. also log model-seed/state if available. if it's nondeterministic we'll need repeatable repro.
ops-bot: Canary deployed: raven-v3-8q -> staging (2% sample). Monitor: /canary/raven-v3-8q/staging
niko: plan for measurement:
- sample 2% production traffic routed to staging
- record: full response text, token count, model-config (quant, temp, max_tokens), route
- attempt parsing client-side; mark parse_status: ok | repaired | failed
- run automatic repair heuristics for "repaired"

elaine: what are the repair heuristics? can you paste the current script?
niko: sure, gist of it:
```
# repair heuristics
1) strip trailing junk after last closing brace
2) try wrapping in array if top-level is missing
3) fix single-quote to double-quote common cases
4) iterative comma removal on the last N tokens
``` 
(note: we avoid heavy heuristics that change semantics)
rajeev: about retries: propose a 2-tier retry budget
- per-request budget: max 2 retries
- per-route/minute budget: 20 retries
otherwise drop and count as failed to avoid thundering
maria: can we implement an exponential backoff: 200ms -> 600ms -> give up? Also track which retry succeeded (partial parsing vs full).
niko: yep. retry policy in YAML for the canary (snippet):
```
sampling_rate: 0.02
retry_policy:
  per_request_max: 2
  per_route_minute_max: 20
  backoff_ms: [200, 600]
logging: [response_text, tokens, parse_status, repair_steps]
``` 
ci-bot: Canary test suite ran: basic schema conformance checks passed on 100 golden prompts (deterministic), 4/100 failed under 8q vs 1/100 on 16-bit.
elaine: that's a notable delta. what's the failure taxonomy on those 4?
niko: breakdown:
- 2x truncated JSON (cutoff)
- 1x extra trailing comma
- 1x missing closing bracket
maria: truncated JSON suggests we should compare token budgets. maybe quantization changed token-level distribution leading to slightly longer outputs for same prompt. can we capture token distributions per model?
rajeev: yes, add token-length histogram to telemetry. also capture output entropy proxy: top-1 probability mass for last token.
niko: added to telemetry. early observation: median token length up ~+1 token on 8q for the golden set.
elaine: repair success rate?
niko: out of those 4 fails, repair heuristics fixed 3 (2 truncation fixes by stripping trailing partial token and reparse, 1 comma fix). final effective parse fail delta is 1/100.
maria: but we can't rely on repairs for production correctness: need to decide whether to accept retry/repair policy as part of canary SLO or declare regression.
rajeev: suggestion: define primary SLO = parse_success_without_repair >= 99.5% on golden plus sampled traffic. If below, consider canary hold.
niko: agrees. current raw parse_success_without_repair on sampled traffic: 98.6% (8q) vs 99.7% (16-bit) across 24h sample.
elaine: that's below the suggested SLO. can we split by route? maybe some routes are more sensitive (longer prefixes, tool-heavy prompts).
niko: done. short summary by route:
- chat-assistant (short prompts): 99.4% (8q)
- code-exec-tool (long prefix): 96.8% (8q)
- rerank-route: 99.9% (8q)
maria: so the regression is concentrated on code-exec-tool. what about enabling higher token cap for that route only or shifting that route to 16-bit temporarily?
niko: options:
1) patch route config to bump max_tokens by +16 for 8q
2) increase per-request retry to 3 for that route
3) fallback routing: if parse fails after repair+retries, route to 16-bit variant automatically
rajeev: prefer (3) fallback routing + telemetry. keeps user impact minimal and isolates the cause.
elaine: agree. implement fallback with cost accounting so we can measure delta cost.
maria: also run a focused offline eval with longer synthetic prefixes to see where quant-induced length changes occur. I'll spin up a bench job.
ops-bot: Fallback route rule created: route(code-exec-tool) -> primary: raven-v3-8q, fallback: raven-v3-16f on parse failure (post-repair+2 retries). Rule ID: fr-4921
niko: test note: make sure we don't double-charge metric tags when fallback occurs — billing team asked to see tag 'fallback=true' on those requests.
rajeev: good call. also add a gauge for retry budget consumption so SRE can alert if per-route minute budget being approached.
maria: running offline bench now. estimated runtime ~45m. will post summary.
elaine: thanks. next steps for canary:
- add token histograms + entropy proxy to dashboard (niko)
- add fallback tag for billing and route guardrails (rajeev)
- run focused bench and share examples of failures (maria)
- hold on global promote until code-exec-tool >= 99.5% raw parse success (no repair)
niko: noted. if anyone sees a sharp spike in parse failures, ping @niko and @maria immediately :phone:
maria: bench finished — initial artifacts uploaded: https://internal.redwood.ai/artifacts/2071567890/bench-8q-vs-16f
niko: looking at artifacts now. thanks everyone.
ci-bot: thread closed by automation after 24h no activity."
